item.text: I’m reviewing the current split to find the next meaningful design improvement, not just move code around. The likely target is separating mutable graph construction from the read-only traversal contract and tightening naming around the demo layer.

I found two remaining design problems worth fixing: mutation is still tied to one concrete graph class, and the traversal utility still carries too much internal state through method parameters. I’m refactoring those next and moving the sample graph out of the entry point.
The refactor is applied. I’m compiling and running again, then I’ll do a quick pass over the updated files to confirm the new interfaces and state object stayed coherent.

I continued the refactor in three directions.

The graph contract is cleaner now: [MutableGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/MutableGraph.java:1) separates mutation from the read-only [Graph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/Graph.java:1) traversal interface, so BFS only depends on what it actually needs. [AdjacencyListGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/AdjacencyListGraph.java:5) now implements that mutable contract and keeps stable unmodifiable neighbor views instead of wrapping lists on every read.

I also tightened the BFS implementation in [BreadthFirstTraversal.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/BreadthFirstTraversal.java:6) by encapsulating traversal state in a private `TraversalState` object. That removes duplicated setup logic and stops the internal algorithm from passing `visited` and `traversalOrder` through multiple helper parameters. The sample graph wiring moved out of `main` into [SampleGraphs.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/SampleGraphs.java:1), leaving [BreadthFirstSearch.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/BreadthFirstSearch.java:3) as a minimal entry point.

Verification passed with `javac *.java` and `java BreadthFirstSearch`; output is still `0 2 3 1 4 5`.

The next worthwhile step would be tests or package-level organization if you want the refactor to keep going.
